Q: How do end-to-end contracts connect browser state, API state and background effects?
A:
A full-stack workflow crosses independently failing components. Define a stable operation identity, authenticated scope, API representation, durable acceptance point and browser ownership rule.

The browser can show a pending action while a worker completes it, but should recover status after refresh or disconnect. Keep generated explanation separate from authoritative business state. An end-to-end check should exercise the real boundary that could fail: stale responses, duplicate submission, denied ownership or an interrupted accepted operation.
Why: A user refreshes immediately after submitting a request. The new page should recover the accepted operation by its stable identity instead of creating another request because the earlier in-memory loading state disappeared.
Risk: A polished frontend can conceal missing durable acceptance and recovery behavior.
Trade: Explicit cross-component identities simplify user recovery at additional state-modeling cost.
Try: Submit, disconnect, refresh and reconcile one operation without duplication.
